newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Challenger lead slips in Moldova presidency count.
newsitem.headline: Challenger lead slips in Moldova presidency count.

text.p: Left-wing challenger Petru Lucinschi was leading President Mircea Snegur in early counting for Moldova's presidential election on Sunday, the head of the electoral commission said.

His lead had narrowed from the first figures given, however. Lucinschi, who is chairman of the national parliament, had 51.79 percent of the vote after 34.3 percent of the run-off ballot had been counted, central electoral commission chairman Petru Railean told Reuters.
Snegur, who has been president since independence in 1991, had 48.21 percent.
The count had yet to start in the capital, Chisinau, where Lucinschi is expected to do well among the former Soviet republic's large and mainly urban Russian-speaking minority.
Votes are counted by hand in the 2,000 or so polling stations and the results are then centralised at district and national level.
Electoral officials declined to explain why results from Chisinau were not yet available but said there had been a similar delay in the first round of voting on November 17.
